example_prompt: Follow status and price changes of my Yango Delivery claims with the change journal instead of a webhook.

cursor.description: A string with the ID of the last change. If the cursor isn't added, all changes with a certain limit will be approved

change_type.description: Change type. Possible values: - status_changed — status change. - price_changed — price change.

current_point_id.description: Integer point ID (int64) generated on the Yango Delivery side. It is in the route_points[].id field. Applicable to source, destination, and return points.

new_status.description: Claim status. To learn more, see Status model (https://yango-delivery.viewer.diplodoc.yandex.ru/en/api/express/claim-process.md)

gotchas: Authenticate with 'Authorization: Bearer <OAuth token>'. The token comes from your Yango Delivery account (log in with the credentials your Yango Delivery manager gives you, Integration tab, Get token). It remains valid indefinitely, but changing the account password invalidates it; an invalid token answers 401 unauthorized.
This is the documented replacement for the deprecated callback. Store the returned cursor and send it on the next call; without a cursor, the docs say all changes are returned 'with a certain limit'.

The docs describe 'the change history of the claim', but the body takes no claim_id and each event carries its own claim_id: the reference doesn't say which claims the feed covers. Filter events by event.claim_id.
change_type is status_changed or price_changed; terminal statuses carry resolution success or failed.
The status model also lists pay_waiting (pending payment, with payment on delivery), which the status enum of this reference leaves out: don't reject an unknown status value.

Errors return { code, message }: branch on code. Documented on this endpoint: 400 invalid_cursor; 429 too_many_requests. The error guide adds 401 unauthorized (invalid token) and 500 (try again or change the request).
